newsitem.title: RUSSIA: FORECAST - Russia '98 budget sees 3-5 pct GDP growth.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Russia '98 budget sees 3-5 pct GDP growth.

text.p: Russia's draft budget for 1998 foresees gross domestic product (GDP) growth of three to five percent and inflation at eight percent, Prime-Tass news agency quoted the finance minister's budget chief as saying on Tuesday.
The budget plan is almost finished and will be ready for review by the government in early May, First Deputy Finance Minister Vladimir Petrov told Tass.
He said orders on reforms of communal services, such as housing costs, pensions and the military had been drafted along with the budget.
Petrov said that the question of budget relationships to regional governments had not been addressed yet.
The 1997 budget, for which Petrov is preparing a list of cuts to take account of budget shortfalls, puts GDP growth this year at two percent. The Central Bank says inflation will be about 12 percent.
Finance Minister Anatoly Chubais said budget shortfalls this year could be 100 trillion roubles. Revenues targeted by the budget are 434 trillion roubles.
